messages:
Tom S: Hey team — got an escalation from Acme about streaming completions getting truncated. They say the final JSON object is incomplete and finish_reason is missing. Request-id rid_0a9f, region=us-west1, model=text-redwood-001. They attached a raw SSE capture (see below). They get a valid stream for ~18s then the connection ends mid-object. Can we triage?

Maria L: Thanks Tom. Do we know what client/how they connect (browser fetch, EventSource, our node SDK)? Any proxy in front? Any auth/billing errors?

Tom S: They're using browser EventSource behind Cloudflare CDN + our API gateway. No auth/billing errors. They tried our JS SDK streaming and see same.

Alex G: Paste the raw capture here (redact PII). Also include bootstrap headers (request id, x-forwarded-for, etc) and server logs around the request ts.

Tom S: Raw SSE snippet from customer: 
```
event: message
data: {"id":"cmpl-abc123","object":"text_completion","choices":[{"index":0,"text":"Thanks for that. Here's the summary:\n1. ...\n2. ...\n","logprobs":null,
"finish_reason":null}]}

event: message
data: {"id":"cmpl-abc123","object":"text_completion","choices":[{"index":0,"text":"And final note: the summary is complete","logprobs":null,
"finish_reason":
```
They end with newline then connection closed; final chunk truncated (no closing quote/brace for finish_reason).

Maria L: Hmm looks like last token(s) dropped. Could be network close before final flush. Any proxy 502/timeout?

Anne (SRE): Checking infra metrics now. I see a small spike in upstream resets and 502s at 2026-12-03T14:18:23Z (about when the user reported). Proxy (gateway) logged: 
```
[E] 14:18:23 connection reset by peer while flushing to client id=gw-77
```
Also connection pool had a keepalive burst.

Jay P: Two likely causes: (1) our SSE handler writes the final object but doesn't explicitly flush/terminate with the SSE delimiter (double newline) in some codepaths; if a keepalive heartbeat races with finalization the gateway might close mid-chunk. (2) Cloudflare or the CDN might decide the connection is idle and close without letting the backend finish.

Alex G: Repro steps request: can someone give a curl example to reproduce and a minimal server-side log grep? If we can reproduce locally we can validate.

Tom S: Repro curl they used: 
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=text-redwood-001&request_id=rid_0a9f"\
```
I ran this locally against staging and couldn't repro — must be config-dependent.

Anne (SRE): Grep command suggestions for logs: 
```bash
grep -n "rid_0a9f" /var/log/redwood/runtime/* | sed -n '-10,10p'\
```
From gateway logs I see `upstream_write_timeout` entries around the window.

Jay P: I pushed a small instrumented build to staging to add an explicit final flush and SSE delimiter on finalize. Also added a metric when final chunk size < 256 bytes to catch these partial-close cases. Can we coordinate a canary?

Maria L: Before a code rollout, can we try two immediate mitigations for the customer: (A) set the client to poll (non-stream) for that request as a temp workaround, or (B) have them use a small retry on disconnect and re-request the last N tokens via non-streaming completion id? Do we support last_event_id resume?

Alex G: We don't have robust SSE resume semantics; last_event_id currently not wired for token-level resume. So recommend retry with non-stream. Also, tell them to disable CDN-level keepalive/0-idle for that path if possible, or whitelist the endpoint to avoid buffering.

Tom S: I suggested they switch to the SDK poll endpoint as a quick fix and asked for header dump (X-Request-ID, CF-Connecting-IP, Content-Length). They replied with gateway header: `x-gw-timeout: 30s` and `via: cloudflare`.

Anne (SRE): That `x-gw-timeout: 30s` is a smoking gun. If the gateway imposes a 30s idle timeout and a heartbeat interval equals that, race = closed connection. I'll open a config ticket to increase gateway streaming idle to 120s for streaming routes.

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled — canary patch with explicit final flush will go to staging at 14:50 UTC.

Jay P: Plan for fix: 
- Ensure finalize path always writes a trailing `\n\n` SSE separator and calls flush on socket. 
- Add server-side guard: if connection close detected during write, increment metric and try synchronous retry of final frame (best-effort). 
- Add integ test that simulates proxied keepalive close mid-chunk to assert we either finish the object or return an explicit error event.

Temporary mitigations: 
- Increase gateway idle timeout for streaming routes to 120s (Anne to apply). 
- Recommend customers implement client-side small reconnect/retry with idempotent flows.

Maria L: Customer update draft: "We're investigating; short-term: if you can change to non-streaming or add a retry on disconnect that should avoid truncated output. We're rolling a fix to ensure final token flushes and updating gateway timeouts — ETA 24h. Will follow up once canary results are in." 

Tom S: Customer acked and will try the SDK poll fallback. They've asked for a postmortem once fixed.

Anne (SRE): Action items: increase gateway streaming timeout (ticket GATE-482), enable verbose socket flush logging for streaming canary, and monitor partial-final-chunk metric.

Jay P: I'll own the runtime patch (RUNTIME-337). If canary looks good push to prod with a 2% rollout then 50%.

Alex G: Thanks everyone. Please drop any additional logs into the ticket and tag me. We'll follow up with root cause + customer-facing postmortem after we confirm. :thumbsup:
